diagnostic_evidence.quote: By Theorem \ref{existence_of_rationalFIF}, the fixed point of the IFS $\{I\times K; (L_{j,\epsilon}(t), F_{j,\epsilon}(t,f)), j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}\}$ will be a graph of a $\mathcal{C}^1-$rational cubic trigonometric Fractal Interpolation Function.

issues.failure_explanation: With the defining conditions L_{j,epsilon}(t_1) = t_{j+epsilon_j}, L_{j,epsilon}(t_n) = t_{j+1-epsilon_j}, a reversed segment (epsilon_j = 1) makes L_{j,epsilon} decreasing, so a_j = (t_j - t_{j+1})/(t_n - t_1) < 0 (once the garbled formula for a_j, which uses undefined y_1, y_n and data values f instead of knots t, is corrected to the standard zipper form), and the regime |lambda_j| < a_j has no solution: the paper's parameter class is empty for exactly the reversed signatures it advertises and uses in every numerical example. The C^1 claim cites Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF, whose hypothesis |alpha_i| < a_i^p presupposes positive slopes, and whose matching conditions F_{i,1}(x_n, f_{n,1}) = F_{i+1,1}(x_1, f_{1,1}) hold automatically only because f_{1,1} = d_1 and f_{n,1} = d_n in the classical case; for reversed signatures f_{1,1} = (a_1 d_{1+epsilon_1} - lambda_1 d_1)/(a_1 - lambda_1) differs from d_1 and the matching conditions become nontrivial constraints that the source never verifies. The same sign error makes Theorem thm:positivity's scaling bound lambda_j < min{a_i, ...} vacuous for reversed maps, while the numerical section's prescribed bounds (lambda_1 in [0, 0.1333], etc.) equal min{|a_j|, f_{j+epsilon_j}/f_1, f_{j+1-epsilon_j}/f_n} for the given data, showing the intended condition uses |a_j|; the convergence section's h_j = la_j carries the same wrong sign.

failure_location.quote: and $|\lambda_j| < a_j, j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}$ is the vertical scaling factor.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace a_j by |a_j| in the scaling condition and in Theorem thm:positivity's bound (lambda_j < min{|a_j|, f_{j+epsilon_j}/f_1, f_{j+1-epsilon_j}/f_n}), and re-justify C^1 smoothness for signed slopes by verifying (or imposing) the matching conditions F_{i,1}(x_n, f_{n,1}) = F_{i+1,1}(x_1, f_{1,1}) with f_{1,1}, f_{n,1} as defined in Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF; the paper's numerical bounds already use |a_j|.
issues.overall_effect: The C^1-RCTZFIF existence claim and the positivity theorem's scaling hypothesis do not cover reversed signatures, including the paper's headline example epsilon = (1,1,1,1,1,1); Theorem thm:convergence's smoothness hypothesis and its h_j = la_j step are likewise unsupported for reversed maps.
issues.title: Scaling regime |lambda_j| < a_j is empty for reversed segments (epsilon_j = 1 forces a_j < 0); the C^1 existence claim misapplies Theorem existence_of_rationalFIF and its matching conditions do not hold automatically for reversed signatures
issues.why_classification: A local, standard repair (absolute values) restores the intended regime and all examples, but the cited smoothness theorem cannot be applied as stated to negative slopes, so its matching conditions must be re-verified or added — a contained but nontrivial repair, with no loss of advertised scope once done.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The step |alpha_{j,epsilon} B_0 / q_{j,epsilon}(theta)| <= alpha_{j,epsilon} B_0 / xi requires xi <= |q_{j,epsilon}(theta)|, i.e. xi must be a LOWER bound (min |q|); the source defines xi = max |q|, so |q| <= xi and the inequality runs the wrong way, invalidating the estimate of ||M_{j,epsilon} - M_j||_inf. (ii) The two derivative terms consolidate to (2 l a_j (d_{j+1} - d_j) / (pi q)) [alpha_{j,epsilon} B_1 + delta_{j,epsilon} B_2], since [d_{j+1-epsilon_j} - d_{j+1}] = -[d_{j+epsilon_j} - d_j]; the displayed coefficient [alpha_{j,epsilon} B_1 - delta_{j,epsilon} B_2] has the wrong sign and can be negative, so the bound can fail outright (and a_j < 0 for reversed maps compounds this). (iii) 'Since h_j = la_j, and by Theorem thm:rctfif' is a non sequitur: Theorem thm:rctfif bounds ||phi - psi||_inf and says nothing about ||M_{j,epsilon} - M_j||_inf. (iv) In the final theorem C = q_{j,epsilon}(theta)/xi still depends on j and theta, so the stated bound is ill-formed (likewise psi in C^3[a,b] with undefined [a,b], and ||f_{j+epsilon_j} - f_j|| <= Phi fails for sign-changing data, where it can be 2 Phi). (v) Even taken at face value, the bound (||epsilon||_inf/(1-|lambda|_inf))(C Phi + 4 h eta / pi) does not tend to 0 as h -> 0 when ||epsilon||_inf = 1, and the |lambda|_inf/(1-|lambda|_inf) term persists, so the analysis does not establish the abstract's 'convergence ... to the data-generating function' (a sharper O(h) estimate is available from the source's own identity (alpha B_0+beta B_1+gamma B_2+delta B_3)/q_{j,epsilon} = 1 but is never derived).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the estimate using the exact identity (alpha_{j,epsilon} B_0 + beta_{j,epsilon} B_1 + gamma_{j,epsilon} B_2 + delta_{j,epsilon} B_3)/q_{j,epsilon}(theta) = 1 (eliminating xi) or define xi = min_{j,epsilon,theta} |q_{j,epsilon}(theta)|, correct the derivative coefficient to [alpha_{j,epsilon} B_1 + delta_{j,epsilon} B_2], justify the constant replacement directly (e.g. ||f_{j+1} - f_j|| <= ||psi'||_inf h_j), state C as a genuine constant, and either sharpen the first term to O(h) or add a hypothesis such as |lambda|_inf -> 0 to support the convergence claim.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:convergence's proof is invalid at the core estimate of ||M_{j,epsilon} - M_j||_inf and its statement is ill-formed (C non-constant, xi misused); the abstract and conclusion claims of convergence to phi and to the data-generating function psi are unsupported by the derived bound.
issues.title: Convergence estimate uses xi = max|q| as a lower bound for |q| (wrong direction), has a sign error in the derivative terms, and invokes Theorem thm:rctfif without justification; the stated constant C is not well defined and the bound does not deliver the advertised convergence
issues.why_classification: The error-bound conclusion survives a contained re-derivation using identities already present in the source, and the statement needs only small repairs; but the proof must be redone rather than patched locally, and the advertised convergence-to-psi interpretation must be sharpened or weakened, so it is more than a minor fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, ensuring the above inequalities guarantees that $p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta) > 0$, and hence, by Equation~\eqref{pos_con}, the interpolant $\phi_\epsilon$ remains strictly positive on $[t_1, t_n]$.

issues.failure_explanation: From the referential equation phi_epsilon(L_j(t)) = lambda_j phi_epsilon(t) + p_{j,epsilon}(theta)/q_{j,epsilon}(theta) with lambda_j >= 0, positivity of phi_epsilon(L_j(t)) follows from p_{j,epsilon}/q_{j,epsilon} > 0 only under the assumption phi_epsilon(t) >= 0 on all of [t_1, t_n] — which is exactly the conclusion. Chaining the proved implication (conditions imply p_{j,epsilon}/q_{j,epsilon} > 0) with this reduction yields only 'conditions and phi_epsilon >= 0 imply phi_epsilon > 0', i.e. nothing unconditional; no iterate or positivity-preservation argument for the Read-Bajraktarevic operator is given. Separately, the proof's displayed W_{j,epsilon} swaps gamma_{j,epsilon} and delta_{j,epsilon} relative to the construction (W_{j,epsilon} = gamma_{j,epsilon}(f_{j+1-epsilon_j} - lambda_j f_n) - 2l delta_{j,epsilon} d*_{j+1,epsilon}/pi), leaving the proof internally inconsistent, though the final condition happens to match the construction.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t) \geq 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$ and $0 \leq \lambda_j < 1$, it suffices to ensure that the rational term $\frac{p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}{q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}$ is strictly non-negative over the interval.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard bootstrap: take a strictly positive initial function h_0 in C(I) (e.g. the piecewise-linear interpolant of the positive data), show T h_0 = lambda_j h_0 + M_{j,epsilon} > 0 on each I_j using lambda_j >= 0 and p_{j,epsilon}/q_{j,epsilon} > 0, iterate to get T^k h_0 > 0, and conclude h* = lim_k T^k h_0 > 0; also correct the swapped gamma/delta in the displayed W_{j,epsilon} formula.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:positivity is unproved as written: its coefficient conditions are consistent with the construction, but the positivity guarantee currently rests on a circular inference, so the paper's central guarantee (preservation of positivity, relied on by all numerical examples) lacks a valid proof.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:positivity is circular: it assumes the global positivity of phi_epsilon that it is trying to prove
issues.why_classification: The statement and its conditions are consistent with the construction and very likely true, but the proof needs a new (standard yet nontrivial) positivity-preservation argument; no local condition or one-line correction can close the circle.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\psi \in C^3[t_1, t_n]$ be the original function that generates $\{(t_i, f_i),  i \in \mathbb{N}_{n}\}$

issues.failure_explanation: The captions call the plotted curves the 'Classical Interpolant psi', but in the paper's own formal setup psi is the C^3 data-generating function (Theorem thm:rctfif), which is unknown and cannot be plotted; with lambda_j = 0 the RCTZFIF reduces to the classical rational cubic trigonometric spline interpolant phi, a different object, so the captions conflate the reference spline with the target function.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Relabel the captions as the classical rational cubic trigonometric spline interpolant (e.g. phi with lambda = 0) instead of psi.
issues.overall_effect: Only the interpretation of Figures fig:rctzfif_1e and fig:rctzfif_1f is affected; no theorem, guarantee, or computed value changes.
issues.title: Figure captions mislabel the classical spline interpolant as psi, the unknown data-generating function
issues.why_classification: A one-line relabeling fixes the misidentification; no mathematical content, guarantee, or result is lost.
